turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's eyes flashed with indignation as she recalled the numerous occasions on which Mr. Darcy had wounded her pride, and she wondered how he could now expect her to accept his declarations of love.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's eyes narrowed in indignation as he spoke, his voice laced with a hint of haughty incredulity, as if the very idea of Elizabeth's continued disapproval was an affront to his dignity. It was inconceivable to him, he declared, that she should persist in harboring such strong objections to his character after he had so ardently professed his love for her.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Foolish, obstinate man, to suppose that one or two declarations of love could erase the wounds he had inflicted on her

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Foolish, obstinate woman, to suppose that she could so callously dismiss the sincere professions of a man of his standing and character.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's words were laced with a mix of hurt and indignation, as she reflected on the past, 'It's too late for regrets and professions now, Mr. Darcy; you should have thought of that before you so callously disregarded my feelings.'

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's past mistakes could not be entirely erased by a single act of contrition, however ardent it may have been.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: He has been blind to the hurt he has caused, and now he expects her to forgive and forget at a moment's notice, it seems.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: How could she so callously refuse a man who had risked everything, including his family's good name, to declare his devotion to her, and yet she still harbors such baseless resentment towards him?

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How dare he imply that her feelings are baseless, when he has been the one to consistently disregard her own?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: The audacity of her refusal, when she had been the one to precipitate this crisis by her own obstinacy, was a wonder to behold.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How can he claim devotion when his actions have been nothing but a series of condescending, patronizing, and hurtful behaviors towards her, and now he dares to lecture her on her feelings?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Foolish woman, to suppose that she could inspire such passion in a man of his standing, only to spurn him so callously.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How can he possibly expect her to believe in his sincerity, when he has spent the better part of their acquaintance trying to manipulate her into marrying him?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: It is a gross error, a lamentable misjudgment, on her part, to suppose that she can so cavalierly dismiss a man of his standing, a gentleman of his character, and expect him to be nothing more than a lovesick fool.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How dare he pretend to be shocked by her refusal, when he's been the one to make her feel like a mere plaything all along, a prize to be won in his game of pride and vanity.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: It would seem, then, that she has not yet grasped the gravity of her own situation, nor the depth of feeling that she has inspired in him.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How dare he feign such wounded innocence, when his own actions have been the very cause of her distrust and dislike?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Fie upon her obstinacy, it is a woeful misfortune, indeed, that she is unable to see the truth of his ardent passion.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How can he possibly expect her to believe in his sincerity, when his own behavior has been so utterly at odds with his words?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: It is a singular inconsistency, indeed, that she should be so quick to condemn his past actions, yet so obtuse as to miss the sincerity that now animates his every sentiment.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that he had struggled in vain, that his feelings would not be repressed, and that he ardently admired and loved her.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that it was the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned, and that she could not feel gratitude towards him.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy remarked to Elizabeth that she had given him no reason to expect a favourable reply, and that he had no great interest in her opinion.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth asked Mr. Darcy why he had chosen to tell her that he liked her against his will, against his reason, and even against his character, and whether this was some excuse for incivility.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that she had every reason to think ill of him, and that no motive could excuse the unjust and ungenerous part he had acted in separating her sister from his friend.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth asked Mr. Darcy if he could deny that he had been the principal means of dividing her sister from his friend.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that he had no wish to deny that he had done everything in his power to separate his friend from her sister, and that he rejoiced in his success.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that his character had been unfolded in the recital she received from Mr. Wickham, and that she had never desired his good opinion.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy observed to Elizabeth that she took an eager interest in Mr. Wickham's concerns.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that anyone who knew Mr. Wickham's misfortunes could not help feeling an interest in him.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy exclaimed to Elizabeth that Mr. Wickham's misfortunes were indeed great.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy confirmed to Elizabeth that Mr. Wickham's misfortunes had been great indeed.
